items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: I am replacing someone who is irreplaceable in the name of Bill Dobbins

ctx.x: So this is maybe an odd question but why do you think the powers that be at Eastman hired you? Because I’m guessing that there were probably quite a few applicants.

I heard there was a lot of applicants and I am replacing someone who is irreplaceable in the name of Bill Dobbins, who has left a legacy in so many ways. Why did they hire me? I can never get into that too much. I do feel this music and the movement of it is in for a big change especially within the institution walls of the young business of teaching jazz at the higher level, which only started fifty years ago or so. And there was a lot of tenure involved and there still is, but that generation is now starting to…

It’s become a large business as well. I remember, I was at SUNY Fredonia and I graduated in ’72 and we had a fine jazz band but there were no classes, there were no jazz professors, there was a struggle to get rehearsal rooms for jazz etcetera, and think of where it’s at now.
